newsitem.title: CHINA: China minister plays down WTO deal prospects.
newsitem.headline: China minister plays down WTO deal prospects.

text.p: China's foreign trade minister on Thursday appeared to pour cold water on European optimism on a possible breakthrough in Beijing's long-stalled drive to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"Their intentions are kind-hearted but the question of China's accession to the World Trade Organisation is not entirely decided by the European Union," Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Wu Yi told reporters.
Wu apparently was referring to what Beijing sees as a "U.S. veto" over its efforts to join the WTO.

European Commission Vice-President Sir Leon Brittan, who is currently in Beijing, said earlier on Thursday he might soon urge the United States to move quickly on China's WTO drive if Chinese leaders reaffirmed a commitment to Europe's position on the issue.

Europe maintains it would be flexible on requirements for China's full implementation of WTO rules. But Beijing had to make clear its commitment to full compliance and show substantial progress on granting access to its domestic markets.
Beijing wants to join under more lenient rules for developing countries while the United States has insisted that the Chinese economy was too big for such treatment.
